title: Mask Adoption Dynamics
description: Simulate how mask-wearing behavior spreads and persists in a population under peer influence, policy interventions, risk perception, and supply/cost constraints.

interactions.name: Peer Influence
interactions.description: Individuals update mask-wearing propensity based on the fraction of masked peers in their social network and observed norms in locations.

interactions.name: Policy Enforcement
interactions.description: Mandates increase the probability of wearing masks; enforcement at locations can impose fines or deny entry to non-compliers.

interactions.name: Information Campaign
interactions.description: Authority messaging raises awareness and risk perception, affecting adoption decisions with a possible delay.

interactions.name: Mask Purchase
interactions.description: Individuals buy masks subject to price, inventory, and budget; retailers adjust prices based on demand and stock.

interactions.name: Contact Events
interactions.description: People meet at locations; if disease dynamics are modeled, mask use lowers transmission probability during contacts.

interactions.name: Distribution Support
interactions.description: Public health authority distributes free or subsidized masks to households or locations, affecting availability and adoption.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Fraction of the population wearing masks at each timestep.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of days until at least 50% of the population regularly wears masks.

metrics.name: peak_adoption
metrics.description: Maximum observed mask adoption rate and the day it occurs.

metrics.name: sustained_adoption_rate_final
metrics.description: Adoption rate averaged over the final 14 days of the simulation.

metrics.name: mandate_compliance_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of individuals complying with a mask mandate when in effect.

metrics.name: adoption_inequality_index
metrics.description: Disparity in adoption rates across socioeconomic or age groups (e.g., Gini or coefficient of variation).

metrics.name: incidence_reduction_optional
metrics.description: If disease dynamics are modeled, percent reduction in new infections compared to a no-mask baseline.

metrics.name: policy_cost_proxy
metrics.description: Cumulative fines issued or public spending on mask distribution and campaigns.
